meta.title: My Japan Trip — Tokyo, Autumn 2026
meta.subtitle: Three and a half weeks in Japan — Tokyo as home base, a Hakone onsen escape, and all the food, arcades and autumn colour I can fit. Land Haneda 2026-10-19.

timeSensitive.action: Japan admits Canadians visa-free for up to 90 days; make sure your passport is valid for the whole trip (ideally 6+ months) and has a blank page. Renew now if it's close.

You have no Japanese health coverage as a tourist — a hospital visit can be expensive. Buy travel medical + trip insurance that covers your Oct 18–Nov 13 dates and keep the policy number/assistance line on your phone.

timeSensitive.item: Register Visit Japan Web (immigration + customs QR)
timeSensitive.action: Create the entry at vjw-lp.digital.go.jp and complete the immigration + customs declarations to get QR codes — it's the fast lane at Haneda. Do it at home, not in the arrivals hall.
Install (but don't activate) a Japan travel eSIM — e.g. Ubigi, Airalo, Sakura Mobile — so you have data the second you land. Alternatively pre-book a pocket-wifi pickup at Haneda.
Check in on the ANA app ~24h before the 16:30 SEA departure, confirm seat 37D, and save the mobile boarding pass. International check-in desks/bag drop close early — aim to be at SEA ~3h before.

Bring a no-foreign-fee card for purchases and a card that works at 7-Eleven (Seven Bank) / Japan Post ATMs for yen. Optionally carry a little yen for the first taxi/konbini so you're not hunting an ATM while jet-lagged.
Check in ~24h before the 21:15 Haneda departure, confirm seat 35D, save the boarding pass. Get to HND ~2.5–3h early for international; keep any tax-free purchases sealed for customs.

bookByTimeline.action: Autumn is peak season — central hubs (Shinjuku, Shibuya, Ueno, Tokyo Station, Asakusa) book up. Lock your main Tokyo stay early; you can leave a night or two flexible for the Hakone trip.
A ryokan with dinner + private/onsen bath for the Nov 4–5 side-trip. Good ones sell out in autumn-leaf season; book with breakfast/dinner if you want the full experience.

If you want a Disney day, buy date-designated tickets on the official site as soon as your date is set — the Halloween→Christmas changeover is popular. Park passes are cheaper and less crowded on weekdays.
teamLab Borderless (Azabudai Hills) and teamLab Planets (Toyosu) are timed-entry and sell out on weekends. Pick a date/slot and buy in advance.

bookByTimeline.what: Ghibli Museum (Mitaka) — tickets go on sale
bookByTimeline.action: Tickets for a given month are released on the 10th of the previous month at 10:00 JST via Lawson and sell out within minutes. For a November visit that's Oct 10 — be online and ready.
The open-air rooftop is the best city view — sunset slots sell out. Book a timed ticket online for a clear-ish evening.
Buy the eSIM (activate on landing) or reserve a pocket-wifi pickup at Haneda so you have data immediately.
If you want Fuji + red maples, the Fuji Excursion train or a highway bus from Shinjuku to Kawaguchiko can sell out on autumn weekends — reserve a seat.

calendar.title: ✈️ Depart Seattle — NH117 SEA→HND
calendar.bookingNotes: ANA NH117, 16:30 departure, seat 37D. Be at SEA ~3h early for international; online check-in opens ~24h before.

calendar.title: ✈️ Land Tokyo — Haneda (HND), NH117
calendar.bookingNotes: Arrives ~19:00. Have your Visit Japan Web QR ready, activate your eSIM, grab an IC card, then Keikyu/Monorail/Limousine into the city.

calendar.title: 🍠 Autumn food season is on
calendar.bookingNotes: Look out for sanma, chestnut (kuri) sweets, new-crop rice (shinmai), oden, and street-roasted sweet potato (yaki-imo) all trip.

calendar.title: 🍁 Koyo peak — Nikko / Oku-Nikko
calendar.bookingNotes: Late Oct–early Nov is peak in the Nikko highlands (Irohazaka, Lake Chuzenji, Kegon Falls). A long but spectacular day trip. Verify the koyo forecast closer.

calendar.title: 🎃 Halloween
calendar.bookingNotes: Shibuya gets very crowded and the ward actively discourages street gathering/drinking — theme parks and bar districts are the friendlier bet.

calendar.title: ✨ Winter illuminations begin (approx)
calendar.bookingNotes: Many light-ups switch on early–mid November (e.g. Yomiuri Land, Marunouchi, Roppongi). Exact 2026 start dates vary — verify each venue.

calendar.title: 🍁 Kawaguchiko Momiji Festival (approx)
calendar.bookingNotes: Fuji views with red maples along the Momiji Corridor, roughly Nov 1–23. Reserve the Fuji Excursion train/bus on weekends. Verify 2026 dates.

calendar.title: 🎌 Culture Day (文化の日) — national holiday
calendar.bookingNotes: A public holiday; some museums are free and there are cultural events. Expect crowds at popular spots.

calendar.title: 🏹 Meiji Jingu autumn festival — yabusame (approx)
calendar.bookingNotes: The shrine's autumn grand festival runs early November with yabusame horseback archery around Culture Day. Verify the exact 2026 schedule.

calendar.title: ♨️ Hakone — onsen & autumn colour (day 1)
calendar.bookingNotes: Romancecar from Shinjuku → Hakone Free Pass loop: Tozan train to Gora, cablecar + ropeway to Owakudani (black eggs, Fuji views), Lake Ashi pirate ship to Moto-Hakone (lakeside torii), then check into the ryokan. See Plan a Day.

calendar.title: ♨️ Hakone → Tokyo (day 2)
calendar.bookingNotes: Morning onsen, then the Hakone Open-Air Museum and Hakone-Yumoto for lunch/souvenirs before the Romancecar back to Shinjuku.

calendar.title: 🍜 Tokyo Ramen Show, Komazawa Park (approx)
calendar.bookingNotes: A big open-air ramen event usually held late Oct–early Nov; buy meal tickets on site. Verify the 2026 dates before going.

calendar.title: 🎄 Tokyo Disney Resort Christmas begins (approx)
calendar.bookingNotes: The Halloween season gives way to Christmas in early–mid November — decorations, parade and merch change over. Confirm the 2026 date and buy a date ticket.

calendar.title: 🍁 Hakone koyo peak (approx)
calendar.bookingNotes: Early–mid November tends to be peak for Hakone's maples around Lake Ashi and the museums. Verify closer.

calendar.title: 🍁 Tokyo parks start to turn
calendar.bookingNotes: Rikugien, Koishikawa Korakuen, the Meiji Jingu Gaien ginkgo avenue and Shinjuku Gyoen colour up from mid-November, peaking late Nov (some may be just after you leave). Evening light-ups at Rikugien if timing lines up.

calendar.title: ✈️ Depart Tokyo — NH118 HND→SEA
calendar.bookingNotes: ANA NH118, 21:15 departure, seat 35D. At HND ~2.5–3h early; keep tax-free purchases sealed for customs.

homeNotes: You're visiting as a tourist on a Canadian passport — visa-exempt for stays up to 90 days, so this is all logistics, no visa paperwork.
Land at Haneda the evening of Oct 19 (NH117) and fly home from Haneda on Nov 13 (NH118) — about 3½ weeks, Tokyo as your base with a Hakone onsen escape in the middle.
Autumn is the sweet spot: expect roughly 10–20°C, cool evenings, the odd rain shower, and the first koyo (autumn leaves) toward early–mid November. Pack layers and a light rain shell.
Cash still matters at small shops, shrines and some restaurants — but IC cards (Suica/PASMO) and contactless cover most trains, konbini and chains.
Carry your passport: it's your ID and it's required for tax-free shopping (spend ≥¥5,000 at a Tax-Free counter and the 10% comes off).

top10.tip: Fill in Visit Japan Web before you fly — it's the fast QR lane at Haneda
top10.reason: Doing the immigration + customs declarations at home (not in the arrivals hall) gives you QR codes that skip the paper cards and speed you through.

top10.tip: Get an IC card on day one — Welcome Suica / PASMO, or Mobile Suica in your phone
top10.reason: One tap covers trains, buses, konbini and vending machines. Note the physical-card chip shortage — Welcome Suica or the mobile version are the reliable picks.

top10.tip: Book the timed tickets that sell out before you arrive
top10.reason: Ghibli Museum releases on the 10th of the prior month (10:00 JST) and sells out in minutes; teamLab, Shibuya Sky and Disney are date-specific.

top10.tip: Base yourself on the Yamanote loop (Shinjuku, Shibuya, Ueno, Tokyo, Asakusa)
top10.reason: Everything radiates from that loop; a hub stay cuts transfers and lets you drop bags between neighbourhoods.

top10.tip: Chase autumn colour in the right place at the right time
top10.reason: Nikko and Hakone peak late Oct–early Nov; central Tokyo parks turn late Nov — mostly just after you leave — so day-trip to the mountains for peak leaves.

top10.tip: Use a no-FX card and pull yen from 7-Eleven (Seven Bank) or Japan Post ATMs
top10.reason: Those ATMs reliably take foreign cards 24/7. Avoid airport exchange counters and always decline 'pay in your own currency'.

top10.tip: Tax-free shopping: spend ¥5,000+ at a Tax-Free counter and show your passport
top10.reason: The 10% comes off at the till. Goods must stay sealed/unused until you leave — customs can check the digital record at the airport.

top10.tip: Slot a Hakone onsen night into the middle of the trip
top10.reason: ~85 min from Shinjuku on the Romancecar; the Hakone Free Pass covers the whole scenic loop — train, cablecar, ropeway, pirate ship — plus autumn leaves and Fuji views.

top10.tip: Carry a small trash bag and eat where you buy
top10.reason: Public bins are rare and eating-while-walking is frowned upon; konbini and stations have bins, streets mostly don't.

top10.tip: Download offline tools before you go
top10.reason: Google Maps offline area, the Google Translate JP pack, and your airline app mean transit, menus and boarding passes all work without hunting for signal.

findings.tip: Canadians enter visa-free for up to 90 days
findings.why: Tourism/short stays don't need a visa for Canadian passport holders.
findings.how: Just show your passport; you'll get a landing permission sticker. No work allowed on this status.

findings.tip: Visit Japan Web = the fast QR lane
findings.why: Pre-registering immigration + customs online skips the paper cards.
findings.how: Register at vjw-lp.digital.go.jp ~a week out, complete both declarations, save the QR screenshots.

findings.why: HND is much closer to the city than Narita.
findings.how: Keikyu line (to Shinagawa/Asakusa) or Tokyo Monorail (to Hamamatsucho), or an Airport Limousine bus straight to major hotels.

findings.tip: Activate data before you leave arrivals
findings.why: Maps + translation from the first minute beats hunting for wifi.
findings.how: Turn on your pre-installed eSIM, or pick up a reserved pocket-wifi at the airport counter.

findings.tip: One IC card does almost everything
findings.why: Suica/PASMO tap through trains, buses, konbini and lockers nationwide.
findings.how: Add Mobile Suica to your phone wallet, or buy a Welcome Suica/PASMO at the airport (physical stock is limited due to a chip shortage).

findings.why: Most sights sit on or inside the JR Yamanote circle.
findings.how: Learn the loop's big stops (Tokyo, Shinjuku, Shibuya, Ueno, Ikebukuro); plan days by adjacent stations.

findings.why: Tokyo has almost no 24h trains, and taxis are pricey.
findings.how: Check the last connection in Google Maps before a late night; budget a taxi only as a fallback.

findings.why: Bullet trains need a separate ticket/reservation.
findings.how: Buy at machines/counters or the Smart-EX app; a JR Pass rarely pays off for a Tokyo-based trip.

findings.tip: Carry a cash + IC + contactless mix
findings.why: Cards are widely taken, but small shops, shrines and some ramen counters are cash-only.
findings.how: Keep ~¥10–20k in cash, an IC card for tap, and a no-FX card for bigger buys.

findings.tip: 7-Eleven & Japan Post ATMs take foreign cards
findings.why: Many bank ATMs reject foreign cards; these don't.
findings.how: Use a Seven Bank ATM (in every 7-Eleven) or a post-office ATM, 24/7.

findings.why: Tourists can buy tax-free over ¥5,000 at participating stores.
findings.how: Show your passport at the Tax-Free register; keep consumables sealed until you leave.

findings.tip: Always decline 'pay in your own currency'
findings.why: Dynamic currency conversion bakes in a bad exchange rate.
findings.how: When a terminal offers CAD/USD vs JPY, choose JPY every time.

findings.why: Service is included; tipping can cause confusion.
findings.how: Just pay the bill; at sit-down places you often pay at the front register.
findings.impact: One less thing to think about

findings.tip: Ticket machines & table tablets are normal
findings.why: Many ramen/gyudon shops sell meal tickets at a machine by the door.
findings.how: Insert cash/lC, press the picture button, hand the ticket to staff. Point-and-order works.

findings.why: Locals rate on Tabelog; a 3.5+ is genuinely very good there.
findings.how: Cross-check a place on tabelog.com; anything 3.5+ is a strong bet.

findings.why: 7-Eleven/Lawson/FamilyMart do great cheap meals.
findings.how: Onigiri, egg sandwiches, oden, hot snacks, coffee — a solid ¥500 breakfast or late dinner.

findings.why: Autumn has its own menu.
findings.how: Look for sanma (pacific saury), kuri (chestnut) sweets, shinmai (new-crop rice), oden, and street yaki-imo (roast sweet potato).

findings.why: Solo diners are normal and quick at counter seats.
findings.how: For famous or kaiseki spots, book ahead (some via Tabelog/Omakase); otherwise queue or go off-peak.

findings.why: Public bins are rare and streets stay spotless.
findings.how: Carry a small bag; bin it at a konbini, station, or your hotel.

findings.why: No phone calls, keep talk low, bags off seats.
findings.how: Set your phone to silent ('manner mode'); take calls off the train.

findings.tip: Shoes off in the right places
findings.why: Ryokan, some restaurants, temples' inner halls and homes.
findings.how: Watch for a step-up and slippers; socks without holes help.

findings.why: Public baths expect a wash-first, no-swimsuit routine.
findings.how: Rinse thoroughly at the seated showers before soaking; tie long hair up; tattoos may be restricted (check, or book a private bath).
findings.impact: Enjoy the soak, no faux pas

findings.tip: Stand on the left of escalators (Tokyo)
findings.why: People walk on the right in Tokyo (Osaka is the reverse).
findings.how: Keep left unless you're walking up.

findings.why: Leaves peak in the mountains first, the city last.
findings.how: Nikko/Oku-Nikko late Oct–early Nov; Kawaguchiko early–mid Nov; Hakone early–mid Nov; central Tokyo parks late Nov. Check a koyo forecast before you go.

findings.tip: Hakone is the easy onsen + Fuji + leaves day
findings.why: One loop packs a lot in.
findings.how: Romancecar from Shinjuku (~85 min) + Hakone Free Pass for the Tozan train, cablecar, ropeway (Owakudani), and Lake Ashi ship. Stay a night for the onsen.

findings.why: Lakeside views with Fuji behind the colour.
findings.how: Fuji Excursion train or highway bus from Shinjuku; the Momiji Corridor lights up in early–mid Nov. Reserve seats on weekends.

findings.tip: Nov 3 is Culture Day (文化の日)
findings.why: A national holiday — some museums are free and there are events.
findings.how: Expect crowds at popular spots; plan a lighter/indoor day or a museum you've been meaning to see.

findings.tip: It's the tail of typhoon season
findings.why: Late Oct–Nov can still see a storm, and Japan is quake-prone.
findings.how: Enable emergency alerts, grab the JNTO 'Safety tips' app, and check train status if a system's forecast.
